rule.explanation: The prior candidates all increased orders whenever backlog>0 at every node, which raised total cost from 367 to 783 and pushed node2 backlog to 70. The main failure is over-ordering at node2: it has no supplier constraint, so extra orders become inventory/pipeline rather than service, while node0 and node1 starve. This replacement keeps a small, pipeline-aware backlog correction at node0 and node1 only, and relaxes node2 when its pipeline is already large relative to incoming demand. Node0 gets a modest boost to clear its own backlog and replenish the pipeline. Node1 gets a smaller boost only when its backlog is nonzero and its pipeline is not already excessive. Node2 is reduced when pipeline is high relative to incoming, to avoid upstream backlog and cost, and otherwise left near HAPPO.
